## Correctarr
Finds and fixes the problems Radarr, Sonarr, SABnzbd and Prowlarr leave lying around — the ones that sit there because nobody is looking.
A download matched to the wrong film. A release that would be rejected under the custom format rules you changed last month, still downloading under the old ones. An import stuck waiting for manual interaction since Tuesday. A finished file nothing could match to a title. Half a RAR set and 40 GB of debris nobody will ever look at.
The services notice most of this. They just never resolve it.
**27 rules in six areas** — queue, import, library, download client, indexers and the services themselves. For each one you decide what happens when it finds something: report only, remove from the queue, blocklist, blocklist and search again, import, search, or delete. Conditions narrow that down further — *wait at least six hours*, *nothing over 20 GB*, *only when the match is at least 90 % certain* — and a finding that fails one is still reported, with the reason.
A single dry run switch stops every change at once, and it is **on after a fresh install** — everything is found and reported, nothing is touched, until you have looked at the findings and turned it off yourself.
**Guiding principle: when in doubt, do nothing.** A rule that is not sure only reports. Better one finding left alone than one good file thrown away.
- Built-in login, or `AUTH=off` behind Authelia and friends - Works behind a reverse proxy, sub paths included - Notifications through Pushover, Telegram, Discord, ntfy, Gotify or a webhook - English and German interface, following the browser - Setup assistant with a connection test for every service
